title: XAS allocation steering override
description: The typed object a planner's natural language compiles to (§6). One combined override carries all active steering (weights / pins / forbid / lambda / scope / bump); the agent edits it in place and carries it forward each turn. The prompt moves weights and pins; it NEVER edits solver code. Same inputs + same override => byte-identical plan. All dates are ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

pins.description: Instruction-driven pins. 'defer' unpins an order and forbids arrivals before not_before.

order.description: Real order_id / SO line id (resolved from NL by the agent), e.g. 'SO-4000'.

boosts.description: Multiplicative weight bumps on W(o) for a customer's orders.

customer.description: customer_id (resolved from a dealer name, e.g. 'Colmobil' -> CUST-001).

forbid.description: Hard 'do not move' — pins an order to its incumbent vehicle/date.

lambda.description: Changed-date step penalty for this solve. If null/absent, the λ sweep default applies.

scope.description: General filter that DEFINES the working set: when present, only rows matching ALL given dimensions are re-allocatable and everything else stays pinned. This is how the agent works a slice ('allocate all Colmobil orders for August') and how a fix stays local. Omit/null to fall back to the disrupted set.

customers.description: customer_ids or dealer names to include (e.g. ['CUST-001'] or ['Colmobil']).

po.description: purchase orders to include, e.g. ['PO-150'] — matches rows currently allocated to that PO.

orders.description: explicit row ids or SO ids to include, e.g. ['SO-4000-1'] or ['SO-4000'].

bump.description: Which UNTOUCHED rows the planner has EXPLICITLY authorized the solver to displace to rescue a disrupted row (DECIDE-13). Same dimensions as scope. Never bump an untouched order without this — ASK the planner who may be bumped first. The solver only moves a bumpable row when it lowers total cost, so it prefers low-priority, not-already-rescheduled targets. Omit/null = nobody may be bumped (the default).

time_scale.description: Resolution the solver reasons at and the report speaks in (DECIDE-14). 'days' (default) = exact; 'weeks'/'months' round every gap UP to whole units, so the solver stops distinguishing differences finer than a unit (a coarser, calmer plan) and durations read in that unit. Changes the plan, not just the wording. The hard time fence stays in days regardless.

break_cost.description: Cost to displace an allocation from its current binding (DECIDE-3). 'hard' = a real vehicle (VGR/inventory); 'soft' = a future PO-line slot (VPO). Hard is expensive-but-movable, soft is free. Only an ON-TIME binding costs this to displace; an already-late binding is free to re-allocate (a broken promise protects nothing), so the break prices the bump victim, not the disrupted order being rescued. The solver bumps an on-time hard allocation only when the tardiness saved elsewhere outweighs 'hard' — it is the tunable 'how many weighted late-days is one hard break worth' knob. Omit to use the defaults (hard=200, soft=0). Only the keys present are overridden.

hard.description: Cost to break a hard (real-vehicle) allocation.

soft.description: Cost to break a soft (future-slot) allocation.
